location: Whole channel column + toolbar + sidebar (red usage)
issue: Red is used for about 11 different marks on one screen, so the operator can't tell on air from recording from stop from error at a glance.
evidence: main-expanded Feed 1 column alone has: the picture tally ring, the 'ON AIR · Program' badge, the REC dot pill, the strip's red 'RECORDING' label, the red stop-square record button, and the 'On air in Program' badge. The toolbar adds a red Feed 1 cut pill and a red '■ 12:31 · 2' button. The sidebar has a red camera dot, the red backup dot and the red max marker on the shot timer. The status bar has a REC dot. Crops: /tmp/l4/me-pic1.png, me-strip1.png, me-toolbar.png.
scenario: Mid-meeting, the user glances at the window to check what Zoom is getting. Both columns show red (Feed 2 has REC and a red record button too), so 'which one is live' takes reading rather than glancing.
recommendation: Give each meaning its own shape. Solid red fill and the ring are reserved for ON AIR, meaning what a consumer receives. Recording becomes a small red dot plus neutral text ('REC 12:31' in primary label color, no red 'RECORDING' caption). The record control is a neutral ring with a red dot that becomes a neutral square while recording. Errors use orange or red with an exclamation icon, never plain red text. The shot timer's max marker turns neutral.
alternatives: Keep red for REC and use a broadcast-style amber/red 'PGM' lamp for on air
Recording as a pulsing dot with no other red

location: Picture overlays, top row (524 pt picture)
issue: All four picture corners are permanently filled. On a 524 pt picture the top row (key badge, feed pill, role badge, five-button tool group) leaves about 25 pt free and covers the top of the image. This is the clutter the user asked to reduce.
evidence: Crop /tmp/l4/me-pic1.png: '1' key, 'Feed 1 ⌃', 'ON AIR · Program' and the five tool buttons span the full width. The bottom row is filled too: TC, 'Output ⌃', REC. The r3.js tile() always renders the tool group unless compact.
scenario: During a meeting the user wants to see framing and headroom. The overlays sit right where the talent's head is in a tight shot.
recommendation: At rest show only the identity (feed name with role badge merged, e.g. a red-tinted 'Feed 1 · ON AIR' pill) and REC. Tools, the Output/Source picker, freeze, clean, zoom and detach appear on hover or keyboard focus. The timecode moves into the strip, or appears on hover. Drop the separate '1' key badge; the number can live in the pill ('1 Feed 1') or in the toolbar cut buttons only.
alternatives: One overflow '⋯' glass button at the top right that reveals the tool group
Tool state as a single summary chip ('Zebra · Guides') at rest, full group on hover

issue: The pages disagree on whether the picture tool group is visible at rest. main-expanded and standalone always show it; four-up and monitor-tools show it only on hover.
evidence: four-up legend 5: 'At rest only the name, state, timecode and REC stay visible.' The main-expanded crop shows the tools at rest on both pictures.
scenario: An engineer can't tell which behavior to build, and the user reviewing mockups judges clutter from the busier version.
recommendation: Make hover/focus reveal the rule everywhere (see L4-02), and re-render main-expanded, main-collapsed, standalone, single and program-view.
alternatives: Show it at rest only on the focused tile

issue: Cutting to a feed can be done from four places in the window, all drawn at once: toolbar cut pills, clicking the picture, the strip 'Cut to Feed 2 ⌃2' button, and the ⌃1/⌃2 hints in the sidebar. Each repeats the same red/green state.
evidence: main-expanded toolbar ('1 Feed 1' red, '2 Feed 2' green outline), picture tally rings, the strip Output row ('On air in Program' badge, 'Cut to Feed 2' button), sidebar camera rows with ⌃1/⌃2. Crop /tmp/l4/me-strip-row.png.
scenario: The tally state is drawn three to four times. That adds noise, and it makes the meaning of clicking each element less obvious (see S1).
recommendation: Keep one primary cut surface: the toolbar cut buttons, or a cut bar, plus ⌃n. Tally lives on the pictures only. Remove the strip's 'Cut to' button and the 'On air in Program' badge, since the picture ring already says so. Sidebar rows keep only a small tally dot.
alternatives: Keep the strip button and drop the toolbar pills (less central, scales worse to 4 feeds)

issue: One recording is shown up to seven times at the same weight, so the more important 'what is live' signal gets drowned out.
evidence: main-expanded: sidebar camera rows ('REC 12:31' ×2), the sidebar Recording section, picture REC pills ×2, strip elapsed ×2, the toolbar '12:31 · 2', the status bar 'REC 2 feeds 12:31', the menu bar icon dot.
scenario: The user scans for problems. With 'REC 12:31' repeated everywhere, a single orange 'Paused' or 'dropped' is easy to miss.
recommendation: Define one primary place (the strip: elapsed, size, drops) and quiet echoes (a small REC dot on the picture, the status bar summary, the menu bar dot). Remove 'REC 12:31' from the sidebar camera rows and drop the duplicate elapsed time in the toolbar button (show 'Stop All' with a count).
alternatives: Make the status bar the single summary and remove the sidebar Recording section

issue: The most prominent control in the window (filled red capsule) is labelled only with a stop glyph, a time and a bare number. It doesn't say what it does.
evidence: Crop /tmp/l4/me-toolbar.png: the red '■ 12:31 · 2' at the far right. On standalone the same slot says 'Stop All · 12:31', so the label varies by page.
scenario: After the meeting the user wants to stop the backup. It's unclear whether this stops recording, the feeds or the meeting.
recommendation: Label it with its action: 'Record All' when idle, and 'Stop All (2)' plus elapsed time in a quieter secondary style when recording. Consider making it non-filled while recording so the red fill stays exclusive to on air (L4-01).
alternatives: Split it into a 'REC 12:31 · 2' status chip and a separate Stop All button

location: Collapsed strip hover: Stop button next to the stop-square record button
issue: In the collapsed strip's hover state, a 'Stop' button sits right next to the record control, which is already showing a stop square. That's two stop affordances 100 pt apart, plus Pause.
evidence: Crop /tmp/l4/mc-strips.png: Feed 1 row shows '‖ Pause', '■ Stop', a meter, then the red ■-in-ring record button and ⋯.
scenario: The user wants to pause and hits the wrong one. A stopped take can't be undone.
recommendation: The record control is the single record/stop toggle. Pause is a separate secondary icon button. The hover state adds nothing else. The text 'Stop' button is dropped from collapsed rows, or replaces the toggle, not both.
alternatives: Expanded strips only expose Pause/Stop; collapsed shows just the toggle

location: Strip Output row: effect chips + unlabeled switch
issue: The Output row ends with four effect chips and an unlabeled green switch. It's not clear whether the chips are toggles or status, or that the switch is Processing (complete bypass). The most consequential control in the row has no label.
evidence:
Crop /tmp/l4/me-strip-row.png: 'LUT 1080p 4:2:0 29.97' then a bare switch. r3.js strip() renders `
` with no text.
scenario: The user flips the switch to 'turn LUT off' and instead bypasses everything, including the downscale. That changes the output format mid-meeting (S3).
recommendation: Label it ('Processing'), or replace the chips + switch with one 'Effects' pop-up button showing a summary ('LUT · 1080p · 4:2:0') that opens the ordered checklist. Bypass gets a distinct, labelled control. Chips, if kept, need a pressed/unpressed button style distinct from status badges.
alternatives: Chips as status only; edits only via ⋯ popover

issue: Every expanded strip repeats constant information that is the same for all feeds and never changes during a session ('ProRes 422 · clean source', the full camera/device name, 'Live · 2160p 59.94'). That's about 20% of strip text with no operational value.
evidence: Crop /tmp/l4/me-strip1.png: header 'FX3 · Mini Recorder 12G' plus the 'Live · 2160p 59.94' badge, and the folder row's 'ProRes 422 · clean source'. The same appears in Feed 2's strip.
scenario: The strip reads as a dense form instead of a status line, which pushes the user toward collapsing it and losing the useful parts.
recommendation: Show codec/'clean source' once (sidebar Recording section or Settings), and per strip only when it differs. Move the device name to a tooltip or the ⋯ popover. Show the format badge only when it's unusual (e.g. 29.97 vs 59.94 mismatch) or on hover.
alternatives: Keep the device name but drop the format badge (the sidebar already shows it)

issue: Collapsing strips doesn't make the screen calmer. The freed space is immediately filled with two scopes and a director timeline, so the collapsed page has as much ink as the expanded one. With the sidebar visible the pictures are width-limited (524 pt) and can't grow.
evidence: main-collapsed.png: the strips become one line, then a 138 pt scope per feed and a full-width timeline with lanes, speech bars and cut rows. Picture size is identical to main-expanded.
scenario: The user collapses strips to reduce clutter during a meeting and sees no reduction.
recommendation: Define collapse as a calm meeting state. Scopes and the timeline are off by default and are added explicitly (⌥⌘K, View menu). Empty space stays empty, or the pictures grow. Offer 'Focus' (⌃⌘S hides the sidebar) so two pictures grow to about 646 pt. Show this calm state as a mockup.
alternatives: Stacked layout (pictures one above the other) when the window is tall and narrow

issue: With 1–2 cameras the sidebar's camera rows repeat what the strips and pictures show (name, format, REC). The lower third of the sidebar is empty (about 200 pt below Automation on main-expanded), so the sidebar costs 244 pt of picture width for little unique information.
evidence: Crop /tmp/l4/me-sb.png: Cameras rows 'Feed 1 · 2160p 59.94 · REC 12:31'. The full main-expanded.png shows the empty sidebar below the Automation section.
scenario: Two-camera meeting: pictures are 524 pt wide instead of about 646 pt because of a panel whose top section duplicates the strips.
recommendation: Drop or shrink the Cameras section when every camera already has a channel (keep only '+ Add Camera' in the section header). Lead with unique session content (Output/Program, Recording destination, Recent takes, Automation). Consider a narrower sidebar (200–210 pt), and remember the hidden state per layout.
alternatives: Collapse the sidebar to a 64 pt rail by default with 2+ cameras

issue: The collapse-all-strips toggle uses a sliders icon, which reads as 'settings/adjustments'. It sits between the layout picker and Record with no label.
evidence: Crop /tmp/l4/me-toolbar.png: the lone sliders glyph capsule. r3.js toolbar() uses ic('sliders').
scenario: The user looks for display settings, clicks it and the strips vanish. Or they never find the collapse function the legend describes.
recommendation: Use a symbol that means 'compact rows' (e.g. a rectangle.compress.vertical-style glyph) with a 'Compact' label or tooltip, or move it into the View menu only (⌥⌘S) and drop it from the toolbar.
alternatives: Segmented 'Detailed | Compact' control next to the layout picker

location: Program picture + Feed 1 tile both ringed red
issue: In Program view the same image is shown twice with the same red ring: the large Program picture and the Feed 1 source tile. That's double red emphasis on identical content, and it weakens the 'which source is on air' cue.
evidence: program-view.png: the Program picture has a red ring plus 'ON AIR · Zoom'; Feed 1 has a red ring plus 'ON AIR · Program'.
scenario: The eye bounces between two red frames showing the same face.
recommendation: The Program picture gets a neutral frame with a 'PGM → Zoom' label (it is the output, not a source). Tally rings are for sources only.
alternatives: Thin red top bar on Program instead of a full ring

issue: The dropdown is about 700 pt tall with 18–22 rows plus preview. It fits a 13" MacBook Air (about 919 pt usable) with two feeds, but leaves little margin once a banner is added (menubar g) or with 3–4 cameras. Several rows duplicate each other (Stop Feed vs Stop Recording, separate Effects/LUT/Capture Input rows, two automation rows).
evidence: Crop /tmp/l4/single-dd.png: preview plus 17 rows plus the stat line, about 690 pt. In menubar.png, variant (a) has 2 thumbnails plus 14 rows plus the Feed 1 submenu; variant (g) adds two banners.
scenario: Laptop user with 4 cameras and an attention banner: the menu reaches the Dock or scrolls, which NSMenu does with arrows.
recommendation: Fold per-feed rows into one 'Feed 1 ›' submenu per camera (Effects, LUT, Input, Recording). Merge the automation toggles under 'Automation ›'. Cap the top level at about 12 rows, and keep the preview height fixed at about 180 pt.
alternatives: Preview collapsible with a disclosure row
Show the stat line only on ⌥-click

issue: Purple NEW tags appear inline in the UI (sidebar, status bar, dropdown rows, settings rows), often several per screen. They add a fourth accent color and distort the clutter judgement the user is making. Some sit mid-label and wrap ('Record with camera apps' then a NEW tag on its own line).
evidence: Crop /tmp/l4/me-sb.png: NEW after '8TB', after 'Recent Takes', and on a second line under 'Record with camera apps'. Crop me-sbar.png: NEW in the status bar. single-dd.png: two NEW tags in menu rows.
scenario: The user evaluates density with annotation chrome that won't ship, and approves or rejects layouts for the wrong reason.
recommendation: Render a 'production' variant of each key page with NEW tags hidden (a CSS toggle such as body.clean .newtag{display:none}). Mark proposals only in the legend, or with a subtle dotted underline.
alternatives: Keep tags but render them outside the UI as margin callouts

location: Right column: two scopes always on
issue: The everyday one-camera meeting page dedicates a 252 pt column to two stacked scopes (luma plus parade) at rest. That makes the most common, simplest use case look like the busiest technical page.
evidence: single.png: the right column holds Luma Waveform and RGB Parade, full height. The signal path card adds a third information block under the strip.
scenario: A meeting user who never reads scopes sees a control room, which is the opposite of the 'just works in Zoom' path.
recommendation: Default single-camera meetings to the picture only (larger, about 1060 pt wide) with the strip below. Scopes and the signal path appear when toggled. Show that default as the hero for the one-camera case.
alternatives: One scope only, matching the picture tool toggle

issue: A lot of status rides on 10–10.5 pt tertiary-gray text (sidebar sublines, strip folder and time-left, collapsed sizes, status bar), which is hard to read at arm's length on a second display during a call.
evidence: Crop /tmp/l4/me-sb.png: '12:31 · 27.5 GB · ProRes 422' and 'Feed 1_2026-10-20_08-...' at about 10 pt mid-gray. me-strip1.png: '1 h 35 m left' and 'ProRes 422 · clean source' in --label2/--label3.
scenario: The user checks time left on the drive from across the desk and can't read it.
recommendation: Minimum 11 pt for status values, and use secondary (not tertiary) color for anything operational (time left, drops, size). Reserve tertiary for truly decorative captions. L6 should measure contrast.

location: Side margins and the no-signal tile
issue: Four Up uses fixed 574 pt columns, leaving about 70 pt black margins at each side. The No signal tile is a large pure-black block with centered text, the highest-contrast element on the page, so an inactive camera draws the most attention.
evidence: four-up.png: empty gutters left of Feed 1/3 and right of Feed 2/4. Feed 3 is a black tile with 'No HDMI signal'.
scenario: The operator's eye lands on the dead camera instead of the on-air one.
recommendation: No-signal tiles use the window's content fill (not black) with muted text and a smaller icon. Center the grid with symmetric gaps, or let tiles fill the width and letterbox inside each tile.
alternatives: Collapse a no-signal tile to a compact card and give its space to the others

issue: Verdict: CONFIRMED. See L4-01.
evidence: About 11 red marks on main-expanded across sidebar, toolbar, pictures, strips and status bar.
recommendation: See L4-01.

issue: Verdict: CONFIRMED, and the actual count is up to seven. See L4-05.
evidence: Sidebar rows, the sidebar Recording section, picture pills, strip elapsed, toolbar, status bar, menu bar icon.
recommendation: See L4-05.

issue: Verdict: CONFIRMED visually. The toolbar's red '■ 12:31 · 2', the strip 'Stop', the stop-square record button and the toolbar 'Stop' (feed) all use the same ■ glyph for different scopes. See L4-06 and L4-07.
evidence: Crops me-toolbar.png and mc-strips.png.
recommendation: Each stop names its scope ('Stop Recording', 'Stop Feed', 'Stop All (2)'), and ■ is used only on the record toggle.

issue: Verdict: CONFIRMED, plus an inconsistency: Four Up already hides tools at rest. See L4-02 and L4-03.
evidence: Crop me-pic1.png: about 25 pt free in the top row.
recommendation: Show tools on hover/focus only, everywhere.

issue: Verdict: CONFIRMED for 1–2 cameras. In Four Up the sidebar is hidden, so it doesn't apply there. See L4-11.
evidence: Crop me-sb.png.
recommendation: See L4-11.

issue: Verdict: PARTLY CONFIRMED. About 700 pt fits a 13" Air with two feeds, but there's little headroom with banners or 3–4 cameras. See L4-14.
evidence: Crop single-dd.png, about 690 pt.
recommendation: See L4-14.

issue: Verdict: CONFIRMED visually (L7 owns the details). A paused feed gets an orange ring on standalone but no ring on four-up. Collapsed rows show effect chips on four-up/program-view, but hand-built hover rows on main-collapsed drop them.
evidence: standalone.png Feed 2 (orange ring) vs four-up.png Feed 4 (no ring). main-collapsed Feed 1 hover row without chips.
recommendation: Add paused, no-signal and hover states to the r3.js builders and re-render.
